sentences.text: Zhylgaia is considered a modern bird, likely belonging to the Neognathae group, which includes most living birds.
The only known fossils of Zhylgaia are two partial humeri found in an upper Paleocene layer in Kazakhstan.
Zhylgaia was once placed in the artificial group Graculavidae, which included Late Cretaceous and Paleocene shorebirds that looked similar but were not closely related.
In 2008, researchers reclassified Zhylgaia into the family Prophaethontidae because its anatomy and size matched the extinct tropicbird-like Lithoptila.
Zhylgaia lived during the Thanetian stage of the Paleocene, between 59.24 and 56 million years ago.
